messages:
Iris: Seabass-17B int4 QC: initial onboard looks excellent for single-turn L2R tasks, but we see weird slowgen tail spikes and occasional OOMs for interactive chat flows.
Vikram: how frequent are the OOMs? host-level or worker-only?
Iris: worker-only, ~0.08% of requests in stress suite (concurrency 24, mixed prompt lengths). Slowgen p99 occasionally jumps x2. Repro trace below.
Tao: paste logs / perf command.
Iris: run command and excerpt: 
```
rbench --model seabass-17b-int4 --suite chat-sim --concurrency 24 --batch-cap 10 --batch_window_ms 18 --max_new_tokens 600
[2024-11-02T02:04:12Z] gen:start req=0x9f ctx=2048 gen=512
[2024-11-02T02:04:12Z] alloc: need_contig=1.0GB free_contig=650MB total_free=4.2GB
[2024-11-02T02:04:12Z] kv: prefetch queued=12 chunks
[2024-11-02T02:04:12Z] kernel: split_alloc created 29 fragments
[2024-11-02T02:04:12Z] OOM: cannot merge fragments, abort
```
Vikram: looks like fragmentation + large max_new_tokens. Two axes: reduce working set (lower max_new_tokens) and reduce long-lived KV (lower batch_window_ms or prefetch). Also consider per-model allocator hint: reserve_slab=true for int4 to avoid split allocs.
Tao: another lever is adaptive-batching: scale batch_window_ms by context length (long ctx -> smaller window). Could avoid long-lived entries when ctx>2k.
Iris: proposed quick experiments:
- default max_new_tokens -> 320 for chat endpoints
- batch_window_ms -> 10 for ctx>2k via adaptive rule
- prefetch_limit -> min(1024, ctx/2)
- allocator.reserved_slab=true for seabass-int4
Vikram: also worth testing mixed-attention-precision: keep key/value states stored in int8 to lower dequant cost while weights remain int4. Might reduce scratch allocs during generation.
Iris: running small perf: `rbench --model seabass-17b-int4 --suite chat-sim-longctx --concurrency 24 --batch-cap 10 --max_new_tokens 320 --batch_window_ms 10 --prefetch_limit 1024 --allocator.reserved_slab=true`
Release-bot: perf job scheduled -> https://ci.internal/runs/91234
Iris: preliminary after 8k requests: OOMs=0, slowgen p99 down 42% vs prior int4 run, quality (turn coherence) stable within noise. Cost/token still ~2.9x lower vs fp16.
Tao: good sign. Next: canary rollout plan: 8% traffic with adaptive-batching rule and slab reservation. Monitor OOM rate, p99, CPU usage.
Vikram: add rollback triggers: OOMs > 0.05% or p99 spike > 30% or step quality regression > 1.5%.
Iris: adding onboarding note: "int4 chat models: start with max_new_tokens<=320, enable allocator.reserved_slab, adaptive batch_window <=12ms for ctx>2k, prefetch_limit<=1024." Will PR model-config and perf artifact link.
Tao: also add to eval harness a mixed-burst test (many small convos interleaved with long gens) so we catch slot-churn early.
Iris: thanks team, kicking canary now. :rocket:
Release-bot: Canary started: seabass-int4-canary-2024-11-02 -> targets=8% traffic
